elements.before: Independent, going-concern analysis for funeral homes, crematories, and cemeteries across SBA 7(a), SBA 504, conventional and specialty deathcare, and USDA rural capital. This page is our standing read on how the cremation shift compresses revenue per call, why heritage goodwill and preneed backlogs drive value, and the difference between the market study, the feasibility study, and the going-concern appraisal a lender requires.
elements.after: Funeral homes, crematories and cemeteries draw on one market and run on very different economics. Feasibility Study Company prepares their feasibility studies, each grounded in a regional market study, for owners, successors, buyers, developers and the lenders who finance them. The NFDA tally stands at 15,401 US funeral homes,1 most of them family- or privately owned, so many files are acquisitions in which heritage goodwill and the preneed backlog carry the value. The study projects call volume as cremation compresses revenue per call, and tests a going-concern purchase for SBA 7(a) and 504, specialty deathcare, bank and USDA rural lenders.
